chapters.title: Consider Your Ways
chapters.html:
Haggai 1

This House Lies in Ruins

1In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying,

2"This is what the LORD of hosts says: These people say, 'The time has not come, the time for the house of the LORD to be built.'"

3Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet, saying,

4"Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?

5So now, this is what the LORD of hosts says: Consider your ways.

6You have sown much and brought in little; you eat, but never have enough; you drink, but never have your fill; you clothe yourselves, but no one is warm; and he who earns wages earns them for a bag with holes.

7This is what the LORD of hosts says: Consider your ways.

8Go up to the hill country, bring wood, and build the house, so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified, says the LORD.

9You looked for much, and it came to little; you brought it home, and I blew it away. Why? declares the LORD of hosts. Because of My house, which lies in ruins, while each of you runs to his own house.

10Therefore, because of you, the heavens have held back the dew, and the earth has held back its produce.

11I have called for a drought on the land and on the hills, on the grain, the new wine and the oil, on what the ground brings forth, on man and on beast, and on all the labor of hands."

The People Obey

12Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the remnant of the people obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the LORD their God had sent him; and the people feared before the LORD.

13Then Haggai, the LORD's messenger, spoke to the people with the LORD's message: "I am with you, declares the LORD."

14The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did the work on the house of the LORD of hosts, their God,

15on the twenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.

chapters.title: The Latter Glory of This House
chapters.html:
Haggai 2

Be Strong and Work

1In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet, saying,

2"Speak, please, to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, saying:

3Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes?

4So now, be strong, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD; be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest; be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD, and work; for I am with you, declares the LORD of hosts,

5as the word that I cut with you when you came out of Egypt; and My Spirit stands among you. Do not fear.

6For this is what the LORD of hosts says: Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry ground;

7and I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of hosts.

8The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, declares the LORD of hosts.

9The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts; and in this place I will give peace, declares the LORD of hosts."

Holy and Unclean

10On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet, saying,

11"This is what the LORD of hosts says: Ask the priests for instruction, saying:

12If a man carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with his fold touches bread or stew or wine or oil or any food, does it become holy?" The priests answered and said, "No."

13Then Haggai said, "If one who is unclean by a dead person touches any of these, does it become unclean?" The priests answered and said, "It becomes unclean."

14Then Haggai answered and said, "So is this people, and so is this nation before Me, declares the LORD, and so is all the work of their hands; and what they offer there is unclean.

From This Day I Will Bless You

15So now, consider, please, from this day onward: before stone was laid on stone in the temple of the LORD,

16in those days, when one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were ten; when one came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures from the press, there were twenty.

17I struck you with scorching and mildew and hail, all the work of your hands; yet you did not turn to Me, declares the LORD.

18Consider, please, from this day onward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day that the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid, consider:

19Is the seed still in the barn? Even the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive tree have not yet borne. From this day on I will bless you."

Zerubbabel, My Signet Ring

20The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying,

21"Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying: I will shake the heavens and the earth;

22I will overturn the throne of kingdoms and utterly destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations; I will overturn the chariot and its riders, and the horses and their riders will go down, each by the sword of his brother.

23On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, My servant, declares the LORD, and make you like a signet ring; for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of hosts."

Notes

  • vv4–5 "be strong… and work; for I am with you… My Spirit stands among you" — David's charge to Solomon for the first house, Be strong and courageous, and do it… for the LORD God, my God, is with you (1 Chronicles 28:20), given now three times, to governor, priest and people. Ha-davar asher karatti, the word that I cut, is the word for cutting a covenant: the promise made at the exodus still holds. Ve-ruchi omedet be-tokhekhem, My Spirit stands among you, as Isaiah remembers the exodus, Where is He who put His Holy Spirit among them (Isaiah 63:11). The Greek has no the word that I cut with you.

  • vv6–7 "Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth… the treasures of all the nations will come" — od achat me'at hi, word for word yet once, it is a little. Mar'ish, shake, the verb of the heavens and the earth shake (Joel 3:16). The sea and the dry ground as at the crossing, when the LORD made the sea into dry ground (Exodus 14:21). Hebrews gives v6 in the Greek's words, Yet once (Hebrews 12:26). Chemdat kol ha-goyim, the treasures of all the nations, is singular, the desire of all the nations, with a plural verb, u-va'u, they will come; the Greek has the choice things of all the nations. I will fill this house with glory, as when the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD (1 Kings 8:11).

  • vv15–17 "a heap of twenty measures, there were ten… I struck you with scorching and mildew and hail… yet you did not turn to Me" — v17 is Amos's word, I struck you with scorching and mildew… yet you did not return to Me, declares the LORD (Amos 4:9), with hail added. Ve-ein etkhem elai, yet you did not turn to Me, has no verb in the Hebrew: word for word and not you to Me; the Greek supplies return, as Amos has it. Purah, press, is the winepress of Isaiah 63:3.

  • v23 "I will take you, Zerubbabel… My servant… and make you like a signet ring; for I have chosen you" — the word against his grandfather is turned back: though Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were the signet ring on My right hand, yet I would tear you off from there (Jeremiah 22:24). Zerubbabel is of Jeconiah's line, The sons of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son… Pedaiah… The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3:17–19). Avdi, My servant, is what the LORD called David, say this to My servant David (2 Samuel 7:8); the book ends with I have chosen you.
